summary.text: Anna Golladay, a Democratic progressive faith leader and small-business owner from Hamilton County, lost the November 3, 2026 election for the U.S. House in Tennessee's 3rd District to Chuck Fleischmann.
She describes herself as a community builder.

paragraphs.text: Anna Golladay describes herself as a community builder, progressive faith leader, and small-business owner in Hamilton County, the largest county in the district.
According to her campaign website, she lives in Chattanooga, owns a clothing company she started in 2011, and is CEO of a consulting firm that advises faith communities on their buildings and assets.
She says she previously served as an associate pastor at St. Elmo United Methodist Church and St Marks Church in Chattanooga.
She also says she served as a protest chaplain in Chattanooga for many years.
Golladay is vice president of her neighborhood association, according to her Candidate Connection survey, and describes herself as not a career politician.
During the campaign, she ran on cost of living, healthcare access including Medicaid expansion, and environmental cleanup.
She received 40.2% of the vote to Chuck Fleischmann's 57.6%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
